body:
I don't think adding a focus to the Script Editor is needed. It has been like this for a long time, and its probably intentional. Also, no other IDEs I tested have focus outlines around their script area.

Changing the default Script Editor look is also unrelated to the rest of the PR, I think it should be discussed separately.

The code completion should probably use the regular canvas item, not the text canvas item. It doesn't need to be clipped. 
- related https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104953

But maybe it would be better as a popup instead? 
Either way it can be done later, since you want to keep this PR focused.
The Script Editor draws inline objects and needs to use this canvas item instead. So this needs to be public. or maybe it could be passed to the function. See `ScriptTextEditor::_inline_object_draw`.
Why is this draw added here, isn't it already later at line 935?

Honestly this existing logic doesn't make any sense. The offset is just the top and left margins and shouldn't be divided by 2, and the x and y offset logic are different.

I think the y offset can just be set to the top margin here, and then the drawing logic can be adjusted in some areas.
But that would require lots more changes, so it doesn't need to be in this PR.

I believe the purpose of this was because `xmargin_beg` used the normal style so this had to remove the normal margin and replace it with the readonly margin. (See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/45858)
Though I don't know why this is divided by 2, it doesn't make any sense.

So now that `xmargin_beg` uses the correct style, `ofs_x` should just be 0, it can be deleted.
But that may need more changes, and it is already broken, so it doesn't need to be done in this PR.
This if statement can be deleted, like the one for the x offset below was deleted.
There are 5 `draw_rect`s (including this one) in TextEdit draw that need to be updated to use the new `text_ci`.
We can't use the TextEdit CanvasItem because the text is drawn over it. Fixed it by using a new CanvasItem for code completion to make it draw over the text and to not be clipped.
Fixed.
Removed the other line.

We may need to convert it to Popup since it draws behind the BottomPanel when the text size is large and we only clip it horizontally. Using `z_index = 1` may solve this issue but the HScrollBar still draws over it: And it still goes off-screen:
It breaks the unit tests but i can fix them, I have kept them earlier to avoid causing regressions from this PR.

Fixed a bug here where the half line spacing used to offset the text wasn't taken into account, check the video where the issue happens on the left side.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/070b313f-93f2-4da5-a4f2-daab37cea1ed

Note: This will change the return values for `get_pos_at_line_column` and `get_rect_at_line_column`.

Why did you change rtl to not be cached and the rendering server to be cached? 
rtl is cached often since it has more logic to it, and the rendering server singleton doesn't need to be cached.
If it is too long you can use `RS::get_singleton()`.
In that case we can leave it using the text ci, it will have to be made into a popup later. So there is no need to make a separate ci for it.
Why have this part way through the drawing?

This isn't correct, the rect needs to not be filled in. There isn't an add rect without fill on the RS though, so it may need to be something like:

```suggestion
rs->canvas_item_add_polyline(text_ci, {rect.position, rect.position + Vector2(rect.size.x, 0), rect.position + rect.size, rect.position + Vector2(0, rect.size.y), rect.position, }, {theme_cache.search_result_border_color});
```
Or there would need to be changes to RenderingServer, but that would be out of scope.

Same as above, `overtype_mode` determines fill and not antialiasing.
and same with the next `draw_rect`.

See the EditorSetting `text_editor/appearance/caret/type` for block caret mode.
- This sounds kind of like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/79735 but offset the other way.
The cached variable `rtl` was only used once in that code. will use `RS::get_singleton()` for this without caching both of them.
Removed all the cached variables for `RenderingServer`.
I removed it, using `RS::get_singleton()` directly now for the changed lines only to avoid having unrelated changes.
It is used in a loop here.
It looks like this one still needs to be addressed.
